name: Florence Airport, Peretola
before:
Tuscany's second airport after Pisa, and a small one. The terminals are modest: a larger building holding check in, security, duty free, arrivals and gate one, and an older building reached by an airbridge with gates two to eleven and a food court. There are no jetbridges anywhere on the site, so every flight boards by bus. Clients who expect to walk straight onto the aircraft should be told otherwise.

The single runway shapes the whole operation. Monte Morello sits close enough that departures normally use runway 23, which means aircraft taxi back down the runway before taking off, and arrivals turn at the far end and taxi back to the stands. It is slower than it looks on paper.

A replacement is planned. A new terminal with seven jetbridges is expected within the decade, and a new runway is to be built perpendicular to the existing one, running parallel to the A11, with the current strip reduced to a taxiway.
after: Tuscany's second airport after Pisa, and a small one, with a single runway.

claims.note: Tuscany has three airports with scheduled service (OurAirports): Pisa, Florence and Elba (Marina di Campo). In 2025 Pisa handled 5,977,227 passengers and Florence 3,847,658 (Assaeroporti; Eurostat 5,991,608 and 3,843,423). Elba appears in neither table, which lists airports down to a few thousand passengers.
